'''Dimitri Papamoschou''' ({{langx|el|Δημήτρης Παπαμοσχού|}}; born 1959) is a Greek and [[naturalization|naturalized]]-American [[aerospace engineer]] and [[fluid dynamics|fluid dynamicist]]. He is Chancellor's Professor of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at the [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI).<ref>{{cite web |title=Dimitri Papamoschou {{!}} Samueli School of Engineering at UC Irvine |url=https://engineering.uci.edu/users/dimitri-papamoschou |website=engineering.uci.edu |publisher=University of California, Irvine |access-date=13 February 2026}}</ref> He is known for his research in [[compressible flow]], [[turbulence]], and for developing devices that reduce [[supersonic]] [[jet engine]] noise.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dimitri Papamoschou |url=https://supersonic.eng.uci.edu/ |website=supersonic.eng.uci.edu |access-date=13 February 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Papamoschou earned a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering from [[Syracuse University]] in 1981. He joined the [[Guggenheim Aeronautical Laboratory]] and earned a [[Master of Science]] in 1982 and [[Doctor of Philosophy|doctorate]] in Aeronautics in 1987 from the [[California Institute of Technology]]. His work focused on supersonic mixing layers and [[Compressible flow|compressible]] turbulent flows under [[Anatol Roshko]].

==Career==
In 1988, Papamoschou joined the [[University of California, Irvine]] as an assistant professor in the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering. He later became full professor and was appointed chair of the Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering from 2002 to 2005. He also served as associate dean of the [[UC Irvine Samueli School of Engineering]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Papamoschou to Chair Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering {{!}} Samueli School of Engineering at UC Irvine |url=https://engineering.uci.edu/news/2002/7/papamoschou-chair-mechanical-aerospace-engineering |website=engineering.uci.edu |access-date=13 February 2026}}</ref>

His research specializes in high-speed turbulent [[shear flow]], [[Aeroacoustics|jet aeroacoustics]], and noise reduction for aircraft propulsion systems.<ref>{{cite journal |journal=New Scientist |title=Technology: Shroud keeps jet noise under wraps |date=8 February 1997|volume=153 |issue=2068|page=21 |url=https://www.google.com/books/edition/New_Scientist/lgLxAAAAMAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&bsq=dimitri+papamoschou&dq=dimitri+papamoschou&printsec=frontcover |access-date=13 February 2026 |publisher=New Science Publications |language=en}}</ref> Papamoschou has developed experimental and theoretical methods for flow diagnostics and holds several patents in [[jet noise]] [[Noise reduction|suppression]]
